identity.title: Existing Handpick native mount and workbench integration

closure_unit.outcome: Existing Handpick is genuinely mounted and usable in the native workbench in place of a VS Code-like search control.

materialized_acceptance.text: AC201-1: Inspect and bind current existing Handpick canonical source/API/pins and intended native mount to exact inputs. Native mounting is currently UNVERIFIED. Preserve Handpick behavior/ownership; do not substitute a VS Code-like search control or reimplement its owned mechanic.

AC201-2: Coder A coordinates this Handpick/material interaction slice with MT-200 in its material-docking candidate root; it does not create a third GUI coder. Before physical integration, coordinate exact search/backend_client/shared app hook ownership under current custody.

AC201-3: Prove genuine native mount, keyboard open/focus/selection/dismissal, scoped results/actions and empty/loading/error/denied/recovery states. Preserve existing context permissions and model accessibility without widening access.

AC201-4: Separate workflow tester checks Handpick entry/selection and return to editor/CKC/orchestration multi-step work, including icon/scrollbar, IME/DPI and accessibility behavior. An HTML draft, imported screenshot or unmounted component fixture is insufficient.

AC201-5: Handpick remains reachable from the module/feature Settings hierarchy or equivalent system tree where applicable, with its original controls and typed persistence/error/denied states. Its render/client resources use the shared authoritative GPU owner/accountability contract; no independent device/pool/budget bypass.

AC201-6: Real Handpick entry/focus/selection/dismissal, scoped failure/denial and relevant component states are observable through existing internal_diagnostics and correlated standalone Palmistry records without leaking query/project contents or creating new watcher/control authority.
